chunks: Sahl, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Hakim who said:

Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to my father: Indeed, God is too Exalted, too Majestic, and too Magnificent for the full reality of His description to be reached. So describe Him by what He has described Himself with, and refrain from whatever is besides that.

key_terms.فَصِفُوهُ بِمَا وَصَفَ بِهِ نَفْسَهُ: Describe Him as He described Himself — the principle of adhering strictly to Quranic and revealed descriptions of God
key_terms.كُفُّوا عَمَّا سِوَى ذَلِكَ: Refrain from whatever is besides that — prohibition of speculative theological descriptions not grounded in revelation
key_terms.كُنْهُ صِفَتِهِ: The full reality or innermost depth of God's description — the idea that God's attributes in their true essence are beyond human comprehension

ai.seo_question: How should Muslims describe God according to Imam Musa al-Kazim?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) wrote to Muhammad ibn Hakim's father commanding that God must only be described using the very words and attributes He used to describe Himself in revelation. This letter reflects the Shia theological position of tafwid in divine description: humans must not venture into speculative theological descriptions that go beyond what the Quran and authoritative hadith explicitly state. The Imam's use of a written letter (rather than an oral statement) underscores the gravity of this theological directive.

en.hubeali: Sahl, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Hakim who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> wrote to my father: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is more Exalted, and more Majestic, and more Magnificent than that His<sup>azwj</sup> Description be reached. Therefore, described Him<sup>azwj</sup> with what He<sup>azwj</sup> has Described Himself<sup>azwj</sup> with, and refrain from whatever is besides that’.
en.sarwar: 6. Sahl has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Hakim who has said the following.

“Imam abu al-Hassan Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s.) wrote to my father, ‘Allah is far High, Glorious and Great than that one can reach the essence of His attribute. Speak of only those of His attributes of which He Himself has spoken and refrain from attributes other than those ones.’”
